title: UPI PIN doesn’t prove a customer authorised a transaction: Telangana consumer commission
summary:
As per the Telangana State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission (TSDRC) banks have to produce concrete evidence that the account holder consented to the transfer, a UPI PIN doesn't prove customer authorised the transaction.

The post UPI PIN doesn’t prove a customer authorised a transaction: Telangana consumer commission appeared first on MEDIANAMA.
llm_summary: The Telangana State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission ruled that a UPI PIN alone isn’t sufficient proof that a user approved a payment; banks must provide concrete evidence—such as logs, timestamps or device data—showing the account holder’s consent. This decision pushes payment providers to tighten transaction authentication and documentation, ensuring that disputed UPI transfers can be reliably traced back to the customer’s explicit authorization.
